title: Air Commandos overcome Hurricane Sally
description: U.S. Air Force Staff Sgts. Jeffrey Beilman, a criminal investigator with the 1st Special Operations Security Forces Squadron, and Kristeena Beilman, NCO in charge of integrated resilience with headquarters Air Force Special Operations Command, restore their home after Hurricane Sally struck the area at Fort Walton Beach, Florida, Sept. 24, 2020. Hurricane Sally made landfall as a Category 2 storm and left approximately 30 inches of rain and a 6 foot storm surge. (U.S. Air Force video by Senior Airman Dennis Spain)

transcript.text: (soft music playing)
- [Jeffrey] The initial emotion is slight panic
because you're thinking about all the other videos
that you see of a hurricane coming through
and losing everything that you've worked hard for.
- [Kristeena] I was really scared.
I was scared just because my kids were scared.
And you know we're waking up in the middle of the night
because there's a tornado watch
and we have to go to the bathroom,
and realizing it's only 4:00 AM.
We still haven't even been hit by this storm.
(soft music playing)
(soft music playing)
- [Jeffrey] The amounts of rainfall
that happened in our area led to extensive flooding.
We took in probably 20 to 30 inches of rain.
(soft music playing)
- As unfortunate as it has been,
the amount of love and support we've felt
in the last week alone.
Like I could go into tears...
Thank you to everyone.

or "Hey, are you okay?"
Those things matter and we'll forever be grateful for that.
